$description: Prismata's surface vocabulary: the closed set of material compositions a component may be made of, and the prismata.css recipe that implements each. Every catalogue entry names one or more of these in its `surface` field. tools/build-catalogue.cjs refuses an entry naming a surface not listed here, and refuses a surface whose `class` does not exist in core/assets/prismata.css, so a component cannot be specified in a material Prismata has not published a recipe for.
$rule: The vocabulary is kept small. A component that seems to need a new surface almost always needs one of these on a different element. A new entry here is a new material composition for every platform library, so it is added together with a recipe, a fallback for reduced transparency and forced colours, a contract row in docs/components.md and a changelog entry.

surfaces.name: Plastic foundation
surfaces.use: The root scene or window. One contextual, opaque foundation per view; never a component.

surfaces.name: Frost panel
surfaces.use: Intermediate task frames and every transient surface that opens over content: side panels, drawers, sheets and app bars, and menus, popovers, tooltips and toasts (R15e). Reading content inside it sits on Haze. `.pr-frost.bar` is a transient overlay shaped as a row of controls, a pill with 4px padding: the selection toolbar over highlighted text. `.pane` takes the content radius, for a pane beside content: a navigation rail, a filter panel, a workspace pane. `.flat` drops the grain. `.docked` is a pane docked to the window's edges, with no rim, radius or shadow: an app bar, a sidebar. `.sheet` slides over content from an edge, with the `--pr-edge` rim, the content radius and the float shadow: a drawer. `.reading` holds a Haze reading fill on `::after`, inset by `--pr-frost-reading-inset` (default `--pr-haze-inset`): a toast, a popover. `.flat` composes with `.pane`, `.docked` and `.sheet` (2.7.0).

surfaces.name: Haze reading surface
surfaces.use: Anything read: cards, rows, panels, wells, forms, messages, decisions. 80% fill, 1.95px feather on an isolated paint layer, crisp foreground. `.pr-well` is the same recipe recessed into a Frost or Resin frame. `.pr-haze.overlay` is the recessed overlay: a transient overlay opened inside a pane that is already lifted, drawn as a flat Haze fill with the `--pr-edge` rim and the content shadow, so it can be told from the pane it sits in. `.inset` is a reading card with no border box, its fill inset by `--pr-haze-inset` and no shadow under it: an alert, a result, a product card. `.flush` is the same card filled to its own edge: a thumbnail, a slide, a chart node. `.flat` is the fill on the element itself, with no feather and no layer: a list or accordion row. `.flat.sunken` falls back to the alternate surface instead of the surface: a placeholder. `.raised` gives the fill the float shadow: a command palette (2.7.0).

surfaces.name: Resin plane
surfaces.use: One floating Resin plane with no reading fill of its own, pill-shaped unless it is a panel: a player's transport bar, a pinned element, a Resin handle over imagery or between regions. Controls inside it lose their own backdrop filter, because Resin never contains Resin. A plane whose controls are labels to be read holds a Haze fill as well, and is a dock. `.pr-resin.transport` is the media transport: the pill with 4px block and 12px inline padding around its 48px controls (58px tall with its rim), with tabular time readouts, wrapping to a second row in a player narrower than 420px. `.pr-media` is the stage it sits on (the content radius, the letterbox, `--pr-media-aspect` and `--pr-media-fit`), and `.pr-media-bar` is the region inset 12px, or the safe area in full screen, that holds the transport. `.flat` drops the sheen layers, for a plane that is a mark rather than a control: a step or timeline marker. `.divider` is the handle between resizable regions: the Resin fill and blur only, with no rim, shadow or sheen, falling back to the outline colour (2.7.0).

surfaces.name: Resin panel
surfaces.use: The Resin plane with the content radius instead of the pill, for a floating control plane that is a rectangle: a floating window, a media control bar wider than it is tall. Same fill, rim, blur and float shadow; only the geometry changes.

surfaces.name: Resin control
surfaces.use: An action: a Resin shell with the 8px-inset Haze reading pad and the optical sheen. Pill geometry with `.pr-button`, which coats a `button` or an `a`; `.pr-control` coats any element. `.primary` tints the pad, `.quiet` removes it, `.danger` adds the destructive boundary. Selected state is the primary pad plus label weight 800.

partial..pr-button: Element-keyed: `.pr-button` coats a `button` or an `a`. On any other element, wear `.pr-control`, which coats any element.
partial..pr-control: Takes the radius of what it is: the pill comes with `.pr-button`, and a card-shaped control keeps the content radius of the surface it also wears.
partial.button: Takes the radius of what it is: the pill comes with `.pr-button`, and a card-shaped button keeps the content radius of the surface it also wears.

surfaces.name: Field shell
surfaces.use: The Resin surround of a native text entry, with the Haze well the value is read on and the circular field-state badge. The native control keeps its functional boundary and semantics. `.pr-editor` is the editable surface inside a rich text field: the shared prose vocabulary (headings, lists, checklists, marks, insertions and deletions) with the primary caret and a 28% primary selection, distinct from the primary-soft highlight (D-34). `.pr-editor-toolbar` is its toolbar, above the text on a fine pointer and below it, clear of the touch keyboard, on a coarse one. `.block` is the shell as a block that fills its row, for a field laid out in a form (2.7.0).

partial..pr-field-shell.block: The shell's display only: worn with `.pr-field-shell`, which carries the coat.
partial..pr-editor: A part: the document inside the field shell, which carries the Resin surround and the Haze well.

surfaces.name: Compact display
surfaces.use: Small information displays that sit on content: tags, badges, labels, keyboard caps. A Resin shell with the inset Haze pad, 18px radius. Not for anything that opens. Transient overlays are Frost. `.count` is the size for a count: a 20px circle that grows to a pill, filled to its own edge, with no block padding.

partial..pr-tag: The tag's geometry (the pill, the 48px floor, the type size), worn with `.pr-resin-haze`, which carries the coat.

surfaces.name: Stone label backing
surfaces.use: A label over an unknown or moving backdrop: a caption on media, a status bar over a scene. 55% light / 60% dark fill, feathered like Haze, crisp text. `.pr-media-caption` is a caption cue rendered by the library: the Stone backing on a box above the transport, never under it. `.large`, `.larger` and `.solid` are the reader's caption style: a cue 1.25 or 1.5 times the size, and a cue on the opaque surface. `::cue` on a `.pr-media` video is the flat fill for the browser's own renderer, which follows the reader's system caption settings.

partial..pr-stone: Stone backs a label and takes the radius of the element it backs.
partial..pr-media-caption: A part: the outer element positions the cue, and its inner box (`.pr-media-caption > *`) carries the Stone backing and the radius.
partial..pr-media-caption.large: The reader's caption style, larger: `--pr-caption-scale` multiplies the cue's 15px to 28px range on its inner box. Worn with the cue's own recipe.
partial..pr-media-caption.larger: The reader's caption style, largest: `--pr-caption-scale` multiplies the cue's 15px to 28px range on its inner box. Worn with the cue's own recipe.
partial..pr-media-caption.solid: The reader's caption style, solid: the inner box's backing is the opaque surface with no feather, the backing the cue's fallbacks draw. Worn with the cue's own recipe.

surfaces.name: Mirage scrim
surfaces.use: The chromatic diffusion of the real scene behind a modal. Never a content surface; the decision surface above it is Haze. The opaque setting draws it as the flat fallback fill, as reduced transparency does (2.7.0).

surfaces.name: Dialog
surfaces.use: A Haze decision surface over a Mirage scrim, with the float shadow. Modality, focus and dismissal are the product's. The surface does not scroll: `.pr-dialog-body`, worn with `.pr-scroll-frost`, scrolls inside it, so the title stays in view and the edge fade does not dissolve the surface. `position: fixed` is for a native `<dialog>`; on any other element the host positions it.

partial..pr-dialog-body: A part: the scrolling body inside the dialog's Haze surface, which carries the material; the body adds the scroll contract.

surfaces.name: Indicator
surfaces.use: A 20px informational circle painting Haze on an isolated layer, or, as `.pr-indicator.pill`, the primary fill that travels behind the selected segment of a strip (D-37): tabs, a segmented control, the dock, bottom navigation or a toggle button group. The circle is Haze rather than Resin, because it sits on a surface that is often already translucent. Neither is ever the only mark of a selection: the selected segment keeps its label weight, and the circle never marks one at all.

surfaces.name: Status badge
surfaces.use: The semantic ink and surface pair behind a symbol, with words beside it. Status colours are independent of the palette and are never redefined by it.

surfaces.name: Authored bubble
surfaces.use: A Haze message surface with a directional tight corner. `.own` uses the palette's own-content pair.

surfaces.name: Table
surfaces.use: A Resin shell with an inset Haze fill holding the table, with the primary-soft header and the Resin scrollbar. Rows are read on the Haze; sort and selection are announced, and selection is label weight.

partial..pr-table: A part: the table inside `.pr-table-scroll`, which carries the Resin shell and the Haze fill; the table is transparent on it.

surfaces.name: Dock
surfaces.use: A Resin plane with a Haze perimeter, holding labelled controls on one Stone label backing (`.pr-dock-inner`), so every label reads on the same protected ground: a dock of destinations, and the strips that group controls the same way (tab strips, segmented controls, toolbars, command and action bars). The controls inside are transparent; the current or selected one takes weight 800 and the primary fill, whether it is a dock's destination, a tab or a segment. The controls may be buttons, tabs (`[role=tab]`, selected by `aria-selected`), radio labels (selected by `:checked`) or links (current by `aria-current`); only buttons were reached before 2.3.0.

partial..pr-dock-inner: The Stone label backing inside the dock. The dock carries the Resin blur, and Resin never contains Resin, so the inner fill has none.

surfaces.name: Group
surfaces.use: A Resin plane whose controls touch: button groups and split buttons. The silhouette is one pill, the interior corners square off against their neighbours, and a hairline in `--pr-edge` separates them. The children keep their fill and give up their own elevation and diffusion, because the plane is the group's. `.vertical` stacks them. Not a dock: a dock spaces its controls apart on its Haze fill.

surfaces.name: Navigation entry
surfaces.use: An entry in side navigation, a rail or a tree of destinations. It has no material of its own, sits on the panel beneath it, and carries selection by label weight alone. Pill hit area, 44px target. `.stacked` puts the icon above the label for a rail. Adopted from the documentation site's side menu, which docs/components.md names as the reference implementation of selection.

surfaces.name: Bare control
surfaces.use: A control that must not wear the Resin coat because it sits inside a surface that already has one: a disclosure chevron, a chip's remove button, a sort header, a stepper's arrows, a dismiss button on a toast. Prismata paints every button by element, so this class subtracts the fill, the shadow, the backdrop filter and both pseudo-layers. The focus ring and the target floor stay.

surfaces.name: Drag handle
surfaces.use: A bare control with a grip glyph and a lift while dragging. Keyboard drag is the product's; the handle only says it can be grabbed and when it has been.

surfaces.name: Selection control
surfaces.use: Native checkbox, radio, switch and range, styled by element: a Resin box, circle or track with a contained mark, and the marked glass thumb. Semantics stay native. `.pr-choice` is the same box on any element, for a library that keeps the input visually hidden and draws the box itself (2.8.0); `.radio` is the circle, and a switch's track is the box at the track's size with the pill radius. The mark and the selected colour are the component's. `.pr-choice.outline` is the outlined box: the `--pr-outline` boundary, the plain Resin fill and a single inset rim (2.8.0). In opaque mode and under reduced transparency the box, native or not, becomes the surface with no backdrop (2.8.0).

partial..pr-choice: The box alone: the mark inside it and the colour of a selected box are drawn by the component that wears it.
partial..pr-choice.radio: The box alone, round: the dot inside it is the component's.
partial..pr-choice.outline: The box alone: the mark inside it and the colour of a selected box are drawn by the component that wears it.
partial.input[type=range]: A track and a thumb, painted on the slider's pseudo-elements (`::-webkit-slider-runnable-track`, `::-webkit-slider-thumb` and their `::-moz-range-` forms), which this record does not read.

surfaces.name: Native control furniture
surfaces.use: Parts of native controls the browser draws and Prismata tints: select options, the file button. Platform-owned popups keep platform drawing.

surfaces.name: No surface of its own
surfaces.use: Layout, typography, behaviour and drawing components that inherit whatever they sit on. A chart's marks, a divider, a provider.
